name: survfit0
title: Add a time-zero row to a survfit object

origin.description: Utility used by printing and plotting. A curve that does not start at time zero gets a row at time zero with survival 1, cumulative hazard 0 and standard error 0.
origin.details: For a multi-state curve the values of p0 and sp0 fill in the new row. Influence matrices get a leading zero column. Objects already at time zero, or already survfit0, are returned unchanged.
origin.value: A survfit0 object, with the same elements as x plus the time-zero rows.
origin.example:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(survival))
fit <- structure(list(n = 5L, time = c(1, 2, 4, 7), n.risk = c(5, 4, 3, 1), n.event = c(1, 0, 1, 1), n.censor = c(0, 1, 1, 0), surv = c(0.8, 0.8, 0.4, 0.2), std.err = c(0.1, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3), logse = TRUE, type = "right"), class = "survfit")
out <- survival::survfit0(fit)
cat(paste(out$time, collapse = " "), "\n")
cat(paste(out$surv, collapse = " "), "\n")
cat(paste(out$n.risk, collapse = " "), "\n")

translation.description: Utility used by printing and plotting. A curve that does not start at time zero gets a row at time zero with survival 1, cumulative hazard 0 and standard error 0.
translation.details: Pass a survfit object as a dict with the R element names and a class_ tuple, for example ('survfit',). Multi-state pstate is a 3-D array (time, curve, state). Matrices are 2-D arrays with time in rows.
translation.value: A dict with the same keys as x, time-zero rows added, and class_ set to ('survfit0', ...) plus the original classes.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from survival.survfit0 import survfit0

fit = {
    "n": 5,
    "time": np.array([1, 2, 4, 7.0]),
    "n.risk": np.array([5, 4, 3, 1.0]),
    "n.event": np.array([1, 0, 1, 1.0]),
    "n.censor": np.array([0, 1, 1, 0.0]),
    "surv": np.array([0.8, 0.8, 0.4, 0.2]),
    "std.err": np.array([0.1, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3]),
    "logse": True,
    "type": "right",
    "class_": ("survfit",),
}
out = survfit0(fit)
print(" ".join(f"{v:g}" for v in out["time"]))
print(" ".join(f"{v:g}" for v in out["surv"]))
print(" ".join(f"{v:g}" for v in out["n.risk"]))
